modifier.description:
Value type modifier

Non empty constraint is specified by adding an exclamation mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  where: !Location
```

The desire to preserve empty values (such that they can be differentiated from the lack of any value) is specified
by adding a question mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  approved: ?boolean
```

The non optional function parameter constraint is specified by adding `!?` in front of the ValueType:
```type
  f: function(url: !?string serialized Url)
```

@see #isNonEmpty
@see #preservesEmpty
@see #isNonOptionalParam
@see FunctionParam#isNonOptional

title:
The "void" value type represents that _no_ value is expected. It is declared in DSL simply as `void`.

The only legal value for this type is `null`, but more importantly its use indicates that there will never be a
meaningful value in this context.

This type may be used in the DSL to indicate no value is expected, for example in declaring that a generic binding
will never have a value:
```type
type Pipeline.Step<In, Out>

type Pipeline.Sink<In> mixes Pipeline.Step<In, void>
```

Note that {@link ValueType#guessType} will never return this type; it returns `null` instead. Similarly,
{@link FunctionType#returnType} returns `null` if there is no return value type declared.

This is also not a data type (more of a special marker), so it cannot explicitly be used for a field,
method parameter or return value. These can _implicitly_ become `void` through a generic binding. For example
**Foo** is generic:

```c3typ
type Foo<T> {
  f: T
  getF: member function(): T
  compareToF: member function(v: T): @comparator int32
}
```

A binding of `T` to `void` means the field, `getF` return value, and `compareTo` parameter will all be of void type:

```c3typ
type VoidFoo mixes Foo<void>
```
